**Finding: deviation (Section 13.5, Ownership)**

Section 13.5 largely delivers our preferred position — Developments, including interface coding created solely by Corio, are owned by Corio, and Commerce One assigns any ownership claim to us, with Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software itself (Section 2.8) properly reserved to it.

The problem is the embedded carve-out: *"unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights"*. That transfers IP we create and fund to the vendor, with no perpetual/irrevocable licence back — an assignment of our IP that falls into walk-away territory and fails the fallback.

Redline (validated, ok:true): delete the carve-out so the sentence reads "…shall be owned by Corio, including all intellectual property rights in the Developments."

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: ownership of enhancements to the Software itself is left to future negotiation (acceptable, as the vendor owns its platform), and there is no express customer-data ownership sentence — a minor gap in this hosting structure.
